subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechcorp.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate you walking through the workloads and the cost pressure you're seeing. Quick recap of what we heard and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points / context
- Unit economics are the top priority: current spend on inference is ~ $0.008/token on managed endpoints; goal is ~ <$0.002 per inference (or roughly 4x reduction).
- Peak real-time traffic: ~180–220 TPS with a heavy tail; 60% of traffic is short prompts (<= 128 tokens), 40% are long sessions with multi-turn chat.
- Current stack: AWS SageMaker endpoints + Triton for some models; limited batching in production because of latency concerns.
- Existing constraints: strict P95 latency SLO of 150–200ms for customer-facing flows; procurement timeline targeted for end of Q2.

Success criteria (what FinTechCorp told us)
- Reduce per-call cost materially while meeting P95 latency <= 150ms at 200 TPS.
- Maintain output quality for the underwriting/assistant prompt set (we'll provide a sample eval set).
- Clear PoC acceptance criteria: accuracy/regression tolerance, latency, and cost delta vs current baseline.

Where Redwood can help / technical notes
- Autoscaling + dedicated GPU pools to guarantee throughput at target latency.
- Workload-aware batching: we expect 4–32 dynamic batch sizes depending on seq length; prefix/KV caching for multi-turn sessions to reduce redundant compute.
- Quantization: many customers get good perf/price wins with 4-bit or 8-bit quantized weights; we'll run quality checks on your eval set to validate.
- Fallback policy: route to cheaper/quantized variant during normal traffic, fall back to full-precision during edge cases.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short cost-savings estimate based on your rough numbers (redwood-cost-savings-estimate.xlsx).

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60–90 min session with your infra/ML engineers next week (we suggested week of Feb 22).
2) PoC scope doc: we’ll share a mutual action plan and proposed acceptance criteria (attached).
3) You to share: 1 week of traffic distribution, a representative prompt/eval set, and a contact for procurement (Sarah — looped).

If this matches your recollection, we’ll lock in the deep-dive time and put together a concrete PoC timeline.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechcorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 20:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap — that’s accurate from our side. A couple quick clarifications:
- We’re definitely open to 4-bit quantization for the non-core safety-critical prompts; for underwriting we want to run the quality checks first but 8-bit might be our initial target.
- We’d prefer a Dedicated capacity PoC so we can validate throughput under realistic load.
- Procurement timeline: target internal approval by end of Q2; Sarah will lead procurement and pricing discussions.

Please go ahead and propose 2–3 slots for the deep-dive next week. We’ll also share a small sample eval set and anonymized traffic histogram by EOD Friday.

Appreciate it — Alex
